text:
marta: kicked off an adaptive shard-scaling run against canary pool gpu-pool-7. goal: reduce steady-state prefix cache footprint while keeping hit-rate >= baseline. quick notes below.

jas: :eyes: nice — any OOM blips during the run?

marta: no hard OOMs. saw a couple transient allocator spikes during long sequences but they didn't fail requests. overall peak mem down ~2.3GB vs fixed-8-shard baseline.

pranav: can you share the profiler snapshot? I want to see whether the spikes are from workspace growth or from per-shard slab allocations.

cheng: uploaded a short flamegraph and a condensed nvprof summary: https://internal.perf/fg/1825012345 (link). snippet from nvprof: 
```
GPU Memory timeline (sample):
  00:00.10 allocate 4.2GB workspace
  00:00.11 slab grow +1.6GB (shard 5)
  00:00.12 cudaMalloc failed (retry) -> fallback to host staging
  00:00.13 reuse pool borrowed 3.8GB
```

marta: thanks. that cudaMalloc failure corresponds to sequences > 2k tokens hitting the longer workspace path.

jas: hypothesis: the adaptive shard scaler is shrinking shard_count aggressively for low-QPS prefixes which causes more cache fragmentation and more frequent slab grows when a large prefix suddenly appears. fragmentation + workspace spikes -> transient allocation pressure.

pranav: agreed. two levers: (1) add a minimum slab reservation per shard (say 128MB) so shard shrink doesn't fully free then re-alloc; (2) increase workspace reuse pool cap and prefer reuse for allocs < 8GB.

marta: ran a micro-sim with those 2 knobs. command: `./tools/simulate_shard_scaling --trace traces/2026-03-prefix-spike.json --min-slab-mb 128 --reuse-cap-gb 40`

marta: micro-sim results (condensed):
```
config: auto-shard, ttl=1800s -> auto 3..14 shards
peak_mem: baseline 22.4GB -> adaptive + knobs 20.1GB
kv_hit: 0.68 -> 0.70
transient_spike_count: 18 -> 4
request_errors: 0 -> 0
```

pranav: nice. 4 transient spikes is acceptable at canary; we should still avoid any path that causes staging to host since that increases latency variance. Consider bumping min-slab if we see host fallbacks in staging.

cheng: also looks like kernel selection interplay matters: when sequence len > 1k we switch to the fused attention kernel which has different workspace patterns. switching kernel at runtime currently requests an extra temporary buffer for half-precision matmuls. that combined with shard slab growth is what pushed us over.

jas: so we should (A) prefer kernel that uses less ephemeral memory for long sequences even if slightly slower, or (B) adjust our scheduler to route long-seq requests to nodes with empty workspace pool. both doable.

marta: propose rollout plan:
- stage: enable min-slab=128MB and reuse-cap 40GB (staging cluster only)
- canary: enable auto-shard with min-shard=3 and ttl=900s at 20% traffic + allocator knobs
- monitor: kv hit rate, peak mem, transient spike count, any cuda errors.

perf-bot: perf check: kv_hit delta = +0.02, peak_mem delta = -2.3GB, error_rate delta = 0.000 (within rounding). alert suppressed. :white_check_mark:

jas: one more ask — can we add a cheap probe that simulates a 2k-token prefix every 5 minutes to every canary node to catch regressions early?

pranav: added to tasks: `ENG-rt: add long-prefix probe to canary harness`

marta: sounds good. I'll land the staging config change after the morning window. thanks everyone — we should have metrics by EOD. :party_parrot:

cheng: FYI, I'll also instrument kernel selection counts in the perf dashboard so we can correlate kernel choice vs workspace pressure.

marta: excellent. follow-ups: jas -> add probe, prana v-> tweak allocator knobs if staging shows host fallbacks, cheng -> dashboard panels.

jas: ack.

pranav: ack.

perf-bot: deploybot: staging change applied to cluster staging-3 at 2026-03-18T09:12:34Z.
